title: T. rex Took 40 Years to Reach Full Size
hook: We picture T. rex bulking up fast. A study of 17 fossils says the opposite: the eight-ton predator may have taken about 40 years to reach full size — a slow, decades-long build.
key_points: A new study re-examined growth across 17 tyrannosaur fossils.
It concludes T. rex likely took about 40 years to reach full size.
Full-grown, the predator weighed roughly eight tons.
That extends earlier growth estimates by about 15 years.
A slower build means a longer adolescence than scientists had assumed.
content_html: Tyrannosaurus rex is the poster child for fearsome speed, so it's easy to assume it grew up fast too. A new study reported via ScienceDaily suggests the opposite: the giant predator may have been a remarkably slow grower.
extra_html: By examining growth recorded across 17 tyrannosaur fossils, researchers estimate that T. rex took about 40 years to reach its full size of roughly eight tons — extending previous estimates by some 15 years. A longer growth period reshapes how we picture the animal's life: rather than rocketing to adulthood, T. rex would have spent decades as a still-growing sub-adult before reaching its full, bone-crushing bulk. That has knock-on implications for how the species lived and how its populations were structured, with many years separating a hatchling from a giant. As with much of paleontology, the conclusion is an inference drawn from limited fossils — but a larger sample makes the slow-growth picture harder to dismiss.

related.title: The History of Life
related.hook: Life is about 3.5 billion years old, but for most of that time it was just microbes. Animals, plants, and us are latecomers crowded into the most recent slice of deep time.

related.title: Mass Extinctions
related.hook: Five times in the past half-billion years, life on Earth was nearly wiped out. Each catastrophe reset the course of evolution — and the asteroid that killed the dinosaurs was only the most famous.

flashcards.prompt: What does the new study suggest about how fast T. rex grew?

choices.text: It took about 40 years to reach full size — roughly 15 years longer than thought
It reached full size within its first two years
It never stopped growing throughout its life

flashcards.explanation_html: Studying 17 fossils, the researchers estimate ~40 years to full size, extending previous estimates by about 15 years.

flashcards.prompt: How big was a fully grown T. rex, according to the study?
flashcards.back_html: Roughly eight tons — a true giant, reached only after about four decades of growth.

flashcards.prompt: What evidence did the study draw on?

choices.text: DNA recovered from a living relative

flashcards.explanation_html: The estimate comes from comparing growth across a set of 17 tyrannosaur fossils, not a single specimen.
